claims.claim: The Web is an information system built on the Internet, using linked resources and shared standards.
CERN's 1989 proposal led to the first browser/server prototype in 1990; CERN made the technology freely usable in 1993.
A computer is not defined by one historical machine; claims about the first computer depend on criteria such as electronic, digital, general-purpose and stored-program operation.
Stored-program computers store instructions and data in memory, a major architectural transition in the 1940s.
Movable-type printing existed in East Asia before Gutenberg's mid-fifteenth-century European press.
The Gutenberg Bible was an early major European book printed with movable metal type, not the first printed book in world history.
Electricity is associated with electric charge and is a secondary energy carrier rather than a primary energy source.
Modern generators commonly use electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
Newcomen's practical atmospheric steam engine was installed in 1712 and was used to pump water from mines.
Bardeen and Brattain demonstrated point-contact transistor action in December 1947; the device was publicly announced in 1948.
Semiconductor technology enabled solid-state devices and the transition from vacuum-tube electronics to compact transistor-based systems.
IP provides addressing and packet forwarding while TCP provides reliable, ordered transport; UDP offers a different connectionless service.
Sputnik 1 became the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth when it launched on 4 October 1957.
GPS uses satellite signals and precise timing to estimate receiver position and time.
The first NAVSTAR GPS satellite launched in 1978; the system later became a worldwide civil and military utility.
Paper-making developed in China in the early centuries CE; Cai Lun is associated with an important improvement to its production, not necessarily the first invention of paper.
A surviving historical record of compass use in China dates to around 1119, while knowledge of magnetic north is older.
Scientific inquiry uses observation, testable hypotheses, evidence and revision, but it is not a rigid universal sequence applied identically in every field.
Germ theory consolidated in the nineteenth century through research identifying microorganisms as causes of many infectious diseases.
Fleming observed penicillin's antibacterial effect in 1928, while the Oxford team later developed it into a therapeutic drug.
Algebraic problem-solving predates al-Khwarizmi; his ninth-century treatise helped establish algebra as a distinct discipline and supplied its name.
Zero has both a placeholder role in positional notation and a role as a number in arithmetic.
Indian mathematicians developed the decimal place-value system and important arithmetic rules for zero; the historical record is gradual and complex.
The international Human Genome Project ran from 1990 to 2003 and produced a high-quality reference sequence, not the genome of a single individual.
The 2003 sequence left difficult repetitive regions unresolved; later work, including the 2022 T2T project, filled major gaps.
Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal and biomass, each with distinct technical and environmental characteristics.
Binary is a base-two positional system; digital hardware represents binary information through physical states in electronic components.
The term algorithm is historically connected to the Latinised name of al-Khwarizmi, whose mathematical works helped transmit calculation methods.
Calculus developed over a long period; Newton and Leibniz independently developed systematic forms in the seventeenth century.
The history of the microprocessor includes multiple antecedents and competing definitions; Intel's 4004 was introduced commercially in 1971.
Mendeleev's 1869 periodic system left gaps and predicted properties; the modern table is ordered by atomic number.
Biodiversity includes diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems, and supports many contributions to human well-being.
